cases.title: Hellcat
cases.semanticExcerpt: A '''hellcat''' is a special cosmetic variant of a normal [[cat]] that can be accessed after starting the [[Freeing Evil Dave]] sub-quest of [[Recipe for Disaster]]. During the quest, players must visit [[Evil Dave]] in [[Doris|his mother]]'s basement. There they must use their cat to kill [[hell-rat]]s, which have stolen his [[Doris|mother]]'s special coloured [[Spice (disambiguation)|spices]] which are needed to make the [[spicy stew]] to free him. After your cat catches seven rats, it will become corrupt by the demonic nature of the rats and will suddenly transform into a hellcat.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|date=11 January 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711144008/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|archivedate=11 July 2022|quote=Looks like it's counting 7 like the wiki says, but won't do it if you already have a hellcat of some sort.}} Alternatively, killing the [[hell-rat behemoth]] seven times will yield the same result. [[Kitten|Kittens]] on the other hand, have a chance to turn into hell-kittens on any hell-rat catch.
cases.positiveFunctionExcerpt: A cat at any stage of growth can be a hellcat, and a cat that has become a hellcat will continue to age as normal.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1471451205964607493|date=16 December 2016|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/H0Yfz|archivedate=20 March 2023|quote=[ if a cat changes to a hellcat, does it reset the timer for it becoming overgrown? 🤔] Doesn't look like it, no.}} To get an overgrown hellcat, you must either grow a regular hellcat into one (by having it following you for another 5-6 hours), or have an overgrown cat kill seven hell-rat behemoths. Players who have completed [[Ratcatchers]] can also get wily and lazy hellcats, either by using their regular wily or lazy cats to catch Hell-Rats, or by taking an overgrown hellcat to [[Felkrash]] and having her train it into a wily hellcat.

Players who have completed [[Ratcatchers]] can also get wily and lazy hellcats, either by using their regular wily or lazy cats to catch Hell-Rats, or by taking an overgrown hellcat to [[Felkrash]] and having her train it into a wily hellcat.

A '''hellcat''' is a special cosmetic variant of a normal [[cat]] that can be accessed after starting the [[Freeing Evil Dave]] sub-quest of [[Recipe for Disaster]]. During the quest, players must visit [[Evil Dave]] in [[Doris|his mother]]'s basement. There they must use their cat to kill [[hell-rat]]s, which have stolen his [[Doris|mother]]'s special coloured [[Spice (disambiguation)|spices]] which are needed to make the [[spicy stew]] to free him. After your cat catches seven rats, it will become corrupt by the demonic nature of the rats and will suddenly transform into a hellcat.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|date=11 January 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711144008/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|archivedate=11 July 2022|quote=Looks like it's counting 7 like the wiki says, but won't do it if you already have a hellcat of some sort.}} Alternatively, killing the [[hell-rat behemoth]] seven times will yield the same result. [[Kitten|Kittens]] on the other hand, have a chance to turn into hell-kittens on any hell-rat catch.

Note that any existing hellcats may need to be placed in a menagerie, or transformed back in to an ordinary cat, in order for subsequent cats to be transformed. A hellcat can be turned back into a normal cat of the same colour it was before the conversion at any time by feeding it a [[bucket of milk]].

==Training==
An overgrown cat can be transformed into a [[wily cat]] (both normal and hellcat versions) by talking to [[Felkrash]] in the [[Port Sarim]] [[Rat Pits]]. They can also be given a name by speaking to her, allowing the player to input a combination of any six letters or spaces, but no numbers. Note that the name will be used for every wily and lazy cat the player has.

When the wily hellcat eventually reverts to a lazy hellcat, it can be re-trained into a wily hellcat by repeatedly catching rats (both normal and [[hell-rat]] versions). Around 15 rats have to be caught before players can expect their lazy hellcat to turn wily again.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Kieren|url=https://twitter.com/JagexKieren/status/720134785646129154|date=13 April 2016|archiveurl=https://archive.is/3gsUy|archivedate=21 April 2023|quote=Catch successfully about 15 rats and it should turn soon :)}} If the hellcat does not seem to transform after catching rats for an extended period of time, players can pick up their lazy hellcat and re-drop it to reset the 'training timer', as otherwise it may be possible to keep training them indefinitely to no avail.

It is not possible to re-train a lazy hellcat into a wily hellcat using a [[ball of wool]] to play with them or by stroking it, only by chasing rats.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1560229125830414336|date=18 August 2022|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/47jm5|archivedate=2 March 2023|quote=(...) as far as I can see the thing's plugged into catching vermin only, rather than stroking or playing with wool.}} Likewise, having your cat chase a [[mouse toy]] will not transform it back into a wily one.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1206580641871077376|date=19 December 2019|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/4DPn9|archivedate=16 December 2020|quote=[The wiki currently states the Mouse Toy "can be used to play with your cat, which can turn a lazy cat back into a wily cat". Can you verify?] I don't see any sign of it doing that to lazy cats, but the code suggests that it makes kittens and grown cats occasionally say "Meow" more and perform a 'pounce' animation at it. I don't believe it'll do anything else.}} Lazy and wily hellcats are known to have a hidden activity level that is incremented by catching rats, which will in turn increase their catch rate as it is raised higher.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1648958707370278912|date=20 April 2023|archiveurl=https://archive.is/GlAUV|archivedate=20 April 2023|quote=That legacy code is deeper spaghetti than most, but it looks like they have an activity level tracker that makes you increasingly likely to succeed once it's been raised. Which your first catches would presumably have done.}}

==Combat stats==
When fighting [[hell-rat behemoth|Hell-Rat Behemoth]]s, the [[King rat]], or in the [[Rat Pits]], hellcats have the following combat stats:{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1221515347687366657|date=27 January 2020|archiveurl=https://archive.is/4aRke|archivedate=28 May 2020|quote=[do you know the actual levels for each type of cat?] Attack, Strength, Defence, HP for each...
Kitten: 1, 1, 0, 4
Grown: 4, 3, 0, 6
Overgrown: 3, 5, 0, 10
Lazy: 6, 6, 2, 14
Wily: 12, 8, 2, 12
@OSRS_Wiki}}

Players are only allowed to have one wily or lazy hellcat out or in bank at a time, in addition to one kitten or adult cat, and as many overgrown cats as they wish. You can however have multiple lazy/wily cats by storing them in your [[menagerie]] before training another. Players can store both lazy and wily cats in their menageries. Wily hellcats will not become lazy while in a menagerie.

After your cat catches seven rats, it will become corrupt by the demonic nature of the rats and will suddenly transform into a hellcat.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|date=11 January 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711144008/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|archivedate=11 July 2022|quote=Looks like it's counting 7 like the wiki says, but won't do it if you already have a hellcat of some sort.}} Alternatively, killing the [[hell-rat behemoth]] seven times will yield the same result. [[Kitten|Kittens]] on the other hand, have a chance to turn into hell-kittens on any hell-rat catch.

Players who have completed [[Ratcatchers]] can also get wily and lazy hellcats, either by using their regular wily or lazy cats to catch Hell-Rats, or by taking an overgrown hellcat to [[Felkrash]] and having her train it into a wily hellcat.

A '''hellcat''' is a special cosmetic variant of a normal [[cat]] that can be accessed after starting the [[Freeing Evil Dave]] sub-quest of [[Recipe for Disaster]]. During the quest, players must visit [[Evil Dave]] in [[Doris|his mother]]'s basement. There they must use their cat to kill [[hell-rat]]s, which have stolen his [[Doris|mother]]'s special coloured [[Spice (disambiguation)|spices]] which are needed to make the [[spicy stew]] to free him. After your cat catches seven rats, it will become corrupt by the demonic nature of the rats and will suddenly transform into a hellcat.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|date=11 January 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711144008/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1216127262917058560|archivedate=11 July 2022|quote=Looks like it's counting 7 like the wiki says, but won't do it if you already have a hellcat of some sort.}} Alternatively, killing the [[hell-rat behemoth]] seven times will yield the same result. [[Kitten|Kittens]] on the other hand, have a chance to turn into hell-kittens on any hell-rat catch.

Note that any existing hellcats may need to be placed in a menagerie, or transformed back in to an ordinary cat, in order for subsequent cats to be transformed. A hellcat can be turned back into a normal cat of the same colour it was before the conversion at any time by feeding it a [[bucket of milk]].

==Training==
An overgrown cat can be transformed into a [[wily cat]] (both normal and hellcat versions) by talking to [[Felkrash]] in the [[Port Sarim]] [[Rat Pits]]. They can also be given a name by speaking to her, allowing the player to input a combination of any six letters or spaces, but no numbers. Note that the name will be used for every wily and lazy cat the player has.

When the wily hellcat eventually reverts to a lazy hellcat, it can be re-trained into a wily hellcat by repeatedly catching rats (both normal and [[hell-rat]] versions). Around 15 rats have to be caught before players can expect their lazy hellcat to turn wily again.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Kieren|url=https://twitter.com/JagexKieren/status/720134785646129154|date=13 April 2016|archiveurl=https://archive.is/3gsUy|archivedate=21 April 2023|quote=Catch successfully about 15 rats and it should turn soon :)}} If the hellcat does not seem to transform after catching rats for an extended period of time, players can pick up their lazy hellcat and re-drop it to reset the 'training timer', as otherwise it may be possible to keep training them indefinitely to no avail.

It is not possible to re-train a lazy hellcat into a wily hellcat using a [[ball of wool]] to play with them or by stroking it, only by chasing rats.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1560229125830414336|date=18 August 2022|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/47jm5|archivedate=2 March 2023|quote=(...) as far as I can see the thing's plugged into catching vermin only, rather than stroking or playing with wool.}} Likewise, having your cat chase a [[mouse toy]] will not transform it back into a wily one.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1206580641871077376|date=19 December 2019|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/4DPn9|archivedate=16 December 2020|quote=[The wiki currently states the Mouse Toy "can be used to play with your cat, which can turn a lazy cat back into a wily cat". Can you verify?] I don't see any sign of it doing that to lazy cats, but the code suggests that it makes kittens and grown cats occasionally say "Meow" more and perform a 'pounce' animation at it. I don't believe it'll do anything else.}} Lazy and wily hellcats are known to have a hidden activity level that is incremented by catching rats, which will in turn increase their catch rate as it is raised higher.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1648958707370278912|date=20 April 2023|archiveurl=https://archive.is/GlAUV|archivedate=20 April 2023|quote=That legacy code is deeper spaghetti than most, but it looks like they have an activity level tracker that makes you increasingly likely to succeed once it's been raised. Which your first catches would presumably have done.}}

==Combat stats==
When fighting [[hell-rat behemoth|Hell-Rat Behemoth]]s, the [[King rat]], or in the [[Rat Pits]], hellcats have the following combat stats:{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1221515347687366657|date=27 January 2020|archiveurl=https://archive.is/4aRke|archivedate=28 May 2020|quote=[do you know the actual levels for each type of cat?] Attack, Strength, Defence, HP for each...
Kitten: 1, 1, 0, 4
Grown: 4, 3, 0, 6
Overgrown: 3, 5, 0, 10
Lazy: 6, 6, 2, 14
Wily: 12, 8, 2, 12

[[File:Dagon'hai robes ornament kit detail.png|left|100px]]
The '''Dagon'hai robes ornament kit''' was a proposed reward for the [[Emir's Arena]]. As with all other [[ornament kit]]s it would have been purely decorative, and could be attached to any pieces of the [[Dagon'hai robes]] set.
Once attached, the ornamented item would become untradeable, but the kit could be detached from the item.
